lines.text: A long coast on the Indian Ocean, gold kingdoms inland, centuries of colonial rule and two wars. This is the story of Mozambique.
Inland, the Kingdom of Mutapa took over the lands of Great Zimbabwe, and sold gold and ivory to traders from the coast.
In 1498 Vasco da Gama sailed up this coast, and Portugal began its slow conquest of the land, a rule that would last nearly five centuries.
On a small coral island, the Portuguese built their capital of East Africa, and gave its name to the whole country.
Far to the south, a settlement grew on a great bay. Once called Lourenco Marques, today it is the capital, Maputo.
Ngungunhane, the last emperor of Gaza, resisted the Portuguese until he was captured in 1895 and sent into exile.
Eduardo Mondlane, a scholar, would found the movement for independence, and be killed for it in 1969.
Samora Machel would lead the fight and become the first president of a free Mozambique.
Joaquim Chissano would follow him, and make peace at last with the rebels.
From the streets of Maputo came Eusebio, one of the greatest footballers of his age, a star for Benfica and Portugal.
Graca Machel would become a minister and campaigner, the widow of Samora Machel, and later the wife of Nelson Mandela.
Mia Couto would become the country's best-known novelist, the author of Sleepwalking Land.
In the centre of the country, Gorongosa became a national park, later emptied by war and brought back to life since the 2000s.
In 1962, Mondlane founded FRELIMO, the liberation movement that has governed Mozambique ever since independence.
Two years later FRELIMO went to war against Portugal, ten hard years of fighting in the bush.
Meanwhile, the Portuguese began a great dam across the Zambezi, at Cahora Bassa.
In 1975, after a revolution in Lisbon, Mozambique finally became independent.
Almost at once, a rebel movement, RENAMO, rose against the new government.
Daniel Chapo was born, who would become president in 2025.
Civil war broke out and lasted fifteen years, devastating the country.
In 1992, in Rome, the two sides signed a peace that ended the war.
But in 2017, a jihadist insurgency broke out in Cabo Delgado, in the far north.
And in 2019, Cyclone Idai struck the coast and flooded the city of Beira.
Through conquest, war and storm, Mozambique has kept rebuilding, facing the ocean.
